prompt:
You are a sceptical financial analyst reviewing a forecast prepared by a colleague.

Given the following forecast for INFY (base year 2022):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2022,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 143534,
      "net_income_cr": 25127,
      "eps": 61.5
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 163029,
      "net_income_cr": 27640,
      "eps": 68.9
    },
    {
      "year": 2025,
      "revenue_cr": 181963,
      "net_income_cr": 30404,
      "eps": 77.2
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Revenue growth moderates from the anomalously high 21.1% YoY in FY2022 (boosted by post-COVID demand surge and digital transformation acceleration) toward the 4-year CAGR of approximately 14.6% (FY2018-FY2022: from 70,522 to 1,21,641 crore), blended with management's sustained large-deal momentum (TCV of USD 9.5 billion), digital revenue mix at 57% growing at ~41% CC, and guidance for continued double-digit growth; a blended projection rate of ~18% for FY2023 tapering to ~14% for FY2024 and ~11.5% for FY2025 is applied as demand normalises post the pandemic-era surge.",
    "Net profit margin is assumed to remain broadly stable at ~17.5%-17.7% of consolidated revenues (FY2022 PAT margin was 18.2% on consolidated basis), with modest compression from continued wage inflation, elevated sub-contractor costs and higher travel resumption, partially offset by operating leverage on a larger revenue base and efficiency gains; EPS dilution is kept minimal given ongoing buyback programme reducing weighted average share count."
  ],
  "reasoning": "FY2022 recorded an anomalously high 21.1% revenue growth on the consolidated P&L (revenues jumped from 1,00,472 crore in FY2021 to 1,21,641 crore in FY2022), driven by a post-COVID demand surge and accelerated digital transformation spending that inflated the latest year-on-year rate well above the 4-year CAGR of ~14.6% (FY2018-FY2022). Accordingly, the latest growth rate alone is not a reliable projection basis, and a mean-reversion approach is applied: FY2023 uses ~18% growth (partial persistence of strong deal pipeline and digital revenue momentum), FY2024 uses ~13.5% (normalisation toward CAGR), and FY2025 uses ~11.5% (steady-state). The 5-year historical data from the key trends table (FY2018: 70,522; FY2019: 82,675; FY2020: 90,791; FY2021: 1,00,472; FY2022: 1,21,641 crore) underpins the CAGR anchor. Balance sheet capacity is strong with consolidated cash and investments of 37,419 crore, minimal financial debt, RoE of 29.1%, and ongoing large capex in land and buildings signalling expansion confidence, supporting a growth rate above pure CAGR."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { — no reasoning or text before the JSON.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}
  ],
  "confidence_score": <0-100>,
  "overall_critique": "<2 sentences>"
}
